title: Can skipped key draws shift a page start?
question: When earlier runes consume extra key draws, does a drift-corrected offset recover a planted key and improve previously reported keys on LP2?
reader_question: Could we miss a correct key by starting too early?
summary: A planted key is recovered only after correcting for skipped draws. Replaying 1,371,030 real-page decodes over 230 previously ranked candidate keys yields no supported reading under the source score gate.
finding: The true key ranks first on all three planted pages at corrected offsets, where its scores are -3.95 to -4.19; uncorrected starts score -6.94 to -7.33. Among 230 candidates across 55 nonempty page starts, the best new corrected score is -6.012 and the best overall -5.885 at a prior restart control; none reaches the source -5.5 reading bar. All 230 source candidate rows replay after a documented staged-input amendment.
limitations: This tests 100-rune page starts under one continuous key-skip law, a score-selected 230-key list, a four-standard-deviation offset band, and a historical English-score gate. It does not exclude other keys, global starting positions, longer segments, or different skip rules.
next_steps: A new key candidate should be tested at predicted drift-corrected offsets with the same planted control, then on held-out page text.

scope.representation: Gematria Primus indices from the source transcription; 55 nonempty LP2-00–55 pages, with source ordinal 52 mapped to LP2-53.
scope.procedure: Run F0 parity gate, replay the three-page planted offset control, and search 230 source-mined key candidates at 5,961 offsets each over first 100 runes of every nonempty page; compare all candidate rows with pinned source output.
scope.parameters: Suppression 0.8129; beam width 400; maximum three skipped draws; predicted key offset start+rho*start with +/-4 standard deviations, plus uncorrected and restart controls; English-score gate -5.5.
scope.exclusions: Keys outside earlier top lists, other global key origins, text after each page first 100 runes, alternate boundaries or filter laws, source B5 skip-count channel.

review.reviewer: F0 parity, three planted rank-one controls, complete source row comparison, independent offset and page-ID arithmetic
